senses.gloss: (b. h., v. זָלַל) to be of slight value, to be cheap; to be despicable, mean.
units: <cite ref="Shabbat 55b:9">Sabb. 55ᵇ</cite> (play on <he>פ̇ח̇ז̇</he>, <cite ref="Genesis 49:4">Gen. XLIX, 4</cite>) <he>פ̇זתה ח̇בתה זַֹלְתָּה</he> (not <cite ref="G00503"><he>זלתא</he></cite>, v. Rabb. D. S. a. l. note 300) thou wast rash, becamest guilty, degradedst thyself.
Snh. 98ᵃ מלכות הַזָּלָה the despicable (Roman) government (Rashi: ‘the slightest trace of tyranny’).—2) (cmp. בּוּז) to squander, be excessive in sensual enjoyments, be dissolute.
Num. R. s. 10 (ed. Amst. p. 240ᵃ) חבורה של זָלִין a company of dissolute men.—Polel זוֹלֵל, only as part.

<cite ref="Midrash Mishlei 2:1-2">Midr. Prov. to II, 4</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="Jeremiah 15:19">Jer. XV, 19</cite>) <he>כל … להוציא ד״ת מז׳</he> he who succeeds in making the words of the Law come forth from a low man (who educates an abandoned person).—
<cite ref="Pesikta Rabbati 21:1">Pesik. R. s. 21</cite> <he>נעשה העולם זוֹלֵלָה</he> the world became an object reduced in value.
Sifré Deut. 219 ז׳ בבשר zolel (Deut. XXI, 20) refers to excesses in eating meat (v.

senses.gloss: to become cheap, fall in price. Y. Keth. XII, beg. 34ᵈ היו ביוקר והֵזִילוּ if provisions were dear and fell in price.

units: <cite ref="Tractate Derekh Eretz Rabbah 2:4">Treat. Der. Er. ch. II</cite> <he>מְזִילֵי הרבים</he> those who treat the public &c. [<cite ref="Bava Batra 25a">B. Bath. 25ᵃ</cite>, v. <cite ref="N00454"><he>נָזַל</he></cite>.]
<cite ref="Mishnah Bava Metzia 5:8">B. Mets. V, 8</cite> <he>והוּזְלוּ</he> and (the wheat) fell.
